originalTitle: Broadcom shares jump over 2% after Apple announces $30 billion chip deal
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: Apple just made a big deal with Broadcom, a company that makes computer chips. As part of the deal, Apple will buy more than $30 billion worth of chips from Broadcom over several years. This is good news for Broadcom, which is why its stock price went up by over 2%. The deal is also important because it will help Broadcom make more chips in the US and support Apple's goal of having a reliable supply of chips made in the country. This partnership will last until at least 2031, which gives Broadcom a steady source of business for many years.

originalTitle: US stocks today: Dow Jones crashes 500 points at open as Trump stops Iran peace deal
simplifiedContent: The US stock market started the day with a big drop, with the Dow Jones index falling 500 points. This happened because President Trump announced that the US is pulling out of a peace deal with Iran, which made investors nervous about what might happen next. As a result, investors are becoming more cautious and selling their stocks, which is causing the market to go down. The price of oil is also going up, which is adding to the market's problems. This all matters because when the market drops, it can affect the value of the investments that people have in the stock market.

originalTitle: HSBC drops 'overweight' call on EM equities on AI spending fears
simplifiedContent: HSBC, a big bank, has changed its opinion on investing in stocks from emerging markets, which are countries that are growing quickly. They were previously very positive, but now they're more cautious due to worries about spending on artificial intelligence (AI) and volatility in Asian markets. This means they think investing in these countries might not be as good an idea as they previously thought, especially in places like South Korea where the stock market has been doing poorly. At the same time, HSBC thinks investing in European stocks might be a better idea, which is why they've become more positive on those. This matters because it could influence how people decide to invest their money.

originalTitle: Wall Street slumps after Trump says Iran deal is ‘over’, Broadcom climbs 3%, United Airlines dips 3.2%
simplifiedContent: The stock market had a bad day after President Trump said that a deal with Iran is no longer in place. When this happened, the main groups of stocks, like the Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite, all lost value. The Dow Jones, which is a group of important stocks, fell by 0.97%, which is a pretty big drop. This matters because when the stock market goes down, it can affect the value of the investments people have in it. Overall, it was a tough day for the stock market, with some individual stocks like United Airlines also losing value, while others like Broadcom actually went up.

originalTitle: Markets tumble after Donald Trump ends ceasefire
simplifiedContent: The stock market had a bad day, with two important measures, the Nifty 50 and the Sensex, falling by 2.1%. This means that the value of the stocks in these measures went down, which can be a sign of uncertainty or worry among investors. The Nifty 50 and Sensex are now at their lowest levels since March 30, which is a significant drop. This happened after Donald Trump ended a ceasefire, which likely caused investors to become nervous and sell their stocks. As a result, the overall stock market lost value, which can affect the investments of people who have money in the market.

originalTitle: Bond yields jump, rupee weakens as oil surges after Trump says Iran deal is over
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: the price of oil has gone up a lot, which is causing some problems. This is because the US President, Trump, said that a deal with Iran is no longer valid. As a result, the value of the Indian currency (rupee) has decreased, and something called bond yields has increased. This matters because higher oil prices and a weaker rupee can lead to higher inflation, which is a concern for India's economy. The increase in bond yields and weakness in the rupee are signs that investors are worried about how these changes will affect the country's finances.
